metadata.case_name: CHAN CHI MING v. SZE HING SANG AND ANOTHER

source: CT thorax, abdomen and pelvis showed multiple rib fracture (right 10th to 12th ribs) and fracture of right transverse processes of L1 to L4. There was also a small right pneumothorax and pleural effusion.
Dr Fu opines that as a result of the accident on 28 July 2008, the plaintiff suffered from ... fracture right 9th to 12th ribs with small pneumothorax.

injuries.description: small right pneumothorax and pleural effusion

injuries.icd_description: Multiple fractures of lumbar spine or pelvis

manifestations.description: pain at his right chest, especially when he straightens his neck backward or raise his head
unable to lie on his left due to the pain in his left chest
persistent pain in his cervical, thoracic and lumbar vertebral especially when he raises his head
aggravated pain in cervical, thoracic and lumbar vertebral after prolonged sitting, standing or walking (about 15 minutes)
intermittent pain in his right knee
very limited movement of neck and back on physical examination (but range observed to be much better when distracted)

treatments_received: pain control by right paravertebral block on 1 August 2008
physiotherapy (magnetic therapy, heat therapy and exercise therapy) - 9 sessions

losses.description: PSLA for residual pain from fractured ribs and related suffering - judge awarded $250,000 for PSLA for residual pain from rib fractures
Inability to return to pre-accident job requiring heavy lifting; must shift to lighter duties such as security guard or cashier; loss of earnings and earning capacity awarded

comparable_cases.case_name: Lam Wai Chun v Tam Chi Wai
comparable_cases.injury_description: 4 fractured ribs. She was hospitalized for some 14 days and was on sick leave for 2 months. She has residual chest pain. After accident, she suffered from adjustment disorder.

comparable_cases.case_name: Chung Chun Man v Chow Wai Kin
comparable_cases.injury_description: Multiple injuries including fractures of 4 right ribs, a right pneumothorax, a right lung contusion, liver laceration and laceration to right flank of the abdomen resulting in haemoperitoneum; exploratory laparotomy revealed small lacerations of the liver and spleen.
